As the imperative is "YOUR turn" then I would agree with Matchstickman that Fanatics turn immediately ends at that point. It's pretty explicit, you draw six cards and then immediately end your turn with everything else in progress failing to complete (there are plenty of precedents with damage dealing stopping before completing eg Wrest the Mind).

If it was put into play by whatever means during another heroes turn then the statement wouldn't have any effect as it isn't Fanatics turn, but that would most likely be a moot point anyway without some kind of card combo chicanery going on.

Spiff's FAQ:

“immediately end your turn” some cards like fanatic’s “prayer of desperation” and nightmist’s “mist-fueled recovery” say to “immediately end your turn”. unlike skipping your turn, where you skip over the end-of-turn phase, when you “immediately end your turn”, you are proceeding immediately to the end-of-turn phase, where you would still do any end-of-turn actions. https://greaterthangames.com/forum/topic/do-prayer-desperation-and-mist-fueled-discovery-skipend-turn

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
You move immediately to your end of turn phase.  That is all, so if Guise has his End of turn shenanigans they would all trigger, you have to deal yourself any damage for Embolden, Zealous offense would destroy itself or not, then your turn is over, then you continue the process.

Just like if an all target damage hits bee bot, you resolve Bee Bot, then continue where you left off, if you still can.

There is no restriction that powers cannot occur outside of your turn, so you would continue the power.

There is one negative.  Smite the Transgressor or Embolden's bonus power use would expire.  If you were hoping to Resolute and give the power to another player and still use Absolution or Martyr by playing Smite the transgressor then using Resolute or having Embolden on Fanatic, you would lose the extra power when your turn ended.

As a bonus Positive, since your turn has ended Vengence Barons Limit of one power a turn would also have expired, which is kind of cool to pull off.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Then would you still get the power use from Transgressor?  Embolden designates power phase, but Smite just says an extra power this turn.

I don't think we've ever had it really spelled out how phases work, but my thoughts have always been that phases aren't periods of time that begin or end, they are points where things trigger.

Your play phase would just be a point of question:  Play a card or skip.  Same with power and draw.

End phase is just the point where all end of turn effects trigger, the end of turn phase wouldn't have a start of the end of turn phase and an end of the end of turn phase, it is a single point that triggers all end of turn effects.  To me it would have no duration at all.

Cards can add a second trigger to end of turn, just like it can add a second trigger to the play phase or power phase.

The way the rules are for the game there really is no reason any phase should have a duration.  Everything we have seems to point to things occuring in instances, and simultaneous resolution for Start of turn and End of turn effects seems to work that same way.

 

This is of course just how I've always seen the game, I don't think anything official has ever gone either way.
